rule: Every visible pixel comes from fetched real game graphics (pret decompilation repos). Only cropping, tile placement per the games' own OAM/frame data, documented flips, position offsets, palette application, backdrop color, and 8x NEAREST upscaling were performed. No pixels were drawn or synthesized.

ref-party-icon-pulse.gif.element: Party-menu Pokémon icon, the continuous 2-frame healthy-state loop (Pikachu)

sources.note: 32x64 indexed PNG: two 32x32 frames stacked vertically

ref-party-icon-pulse.gif.cadence_basis: pokeemerald src/pokemon_icon.c sAnim_0: ANIMCMD_FRAME(0, 6), ANIMCMD_FRAME(1, 6) — 6 ticks at the GBA's ~59.7275 Hz ≈ 100.4 ms per frame (the full-HP cadence)
ref-party-icon-pulse.gif.motion_kind_basis: a two-frame breathing loop: the sprite changes size in place and never travels

deliverables.derivation: Deterministic GIF-to-MP4 media conversion for HTTPS video-reference input; no generated or redrawn frames.

ref-textbox-arrow-bob.gif.element: Message-box down-arrow (▼) vertical bob — motion, not blink
ref-textbox-arrow-bob.gif.cadence_basis: pokeemerald src/text.c: sDownArrowYCoords[] = {0, 1, 2, 1}, delay 8 ticks ≈ 133.9 ms per step (533 ms period)
ref-textbox-arrow-bob.gif.motion_kind_basis: the arrow moves in discrete whole-pixel steps (0/+1/+2/+1) and never rotates or changes shape

deliverables.derivation: Deterministic GIF-to-MP4 media conversion for HTTPS video-reference input; no generated or redrawn frames.

ref-coin-spin.gif.element: Duel coin toss — the full 8-step spin cycle (face → edge → face), metasprite-assembled tile by tile from the game's own frame table

sources.note: AnimData167 sequence (frames 0,1,2,3,4,5,2,6 held 4 ticks each) and AnimFrameTable79 OAM placements (y, x, tile, xflip/yflip) used verbatim

ref-coin-spin.gif.cadence_basis: poketcg anims3.asm AnimData167: each frame held 4 ticks ≈ 67 ms at ~59.7 Hz
ref-coin-spin.gif.motion_kind_basis: the coin turns about its vertical axis in place: face, narrowed, edge, narrowed, face

deliverables.derivation: Deterministic GIF-to-MP4 media conversion for HTTPS video-reference input; no generated or redrawn frames.

ref-item-get-bounce.gif.element: Poké Ball open + sparkle presentation (item-get / release idiom): closed → opening → open, then the field sparkle plays its real 4-frame cycle above the ball

sources.note: 96x16 sheet of six 16x16 cells; sparkle pixels are palette index 14 = pure white, so the backdrop is a dark neutral (96,112,96) to keep them visible — in-game they draw over the overworld scene

ref-item-get-bounce.gif.cadence_basis: pokeemerald src/pokeball.c ball-open AnimCmd steps at 5 ticks ≈ 84 ms; sparkle cells held ~100 ms (6-cell one-shot cycle, middle 4 cells used)
ref-item-get-bounce.gif.motion_kind_basis: a one-shot open-and-present: the ball changes state and a sparkle appears, it does not travel

ref-status-flash.gif.element: Battle status-condition badge (PSN) in a binary on/off alert blink

sources.note: 32x8 PSN strip from the stacked status-icon sheet

ref-status-flash.gif.cadence_basis: Badge art is real Emerald data; in-game the badge itself is static — the on/off blink is the era's binary alert idiom (era corpus §2: 100–250 ms on/off cycling, nothing eases), applied at the textbox 8-tick quantum (134 ms)
ref-status-flash.gif.motion_kind_basis: a binary on/off substitution with no movement of any kind

deliverables.derivation: Deterministic GIF-to-MP4 media conversion for HTTPS video-reference input; no generated or redrawn frames.

ref-ie7-new-tab-insert.gif.element: Tab row while a new tab is opened from the New Tab stub: cursor on the blank stub, the new tab appears fully formed in one frame at the stub position with the stub pushed right, reads 'Connecting...' for ~0.6 s with the page icon, then swaps to its title, gains the close X, and the row re-lays out
ref-ie7-new-tab-insert.gif.kind: screen recording, cropped only (no synthesized pixels); NOT game data — this entry extends the registry to a period browser UI

sources.title: Using Tabs in Internet Explorer 7
sources.note: 640x480 15 fps; crop x0-640 y72-108 of the frame (tab row, video is zoomed in this segment), t=63.6-65.6 s, 2x NEAREST upscale to 1280x72, 30 frames

ref-ie7-new-tab-insert.gif.hold_ms: instant insert at frame 13 (~0.87 s); 'Connecting...' held 9 frames (~0.6 s); title swap at frame 22
ref-ie7-new-tab-insert.gif.cadence_basis: read from the recording at its native 15 fps; the insert spans a single frame (<= 67 ms) — no tween in IE7
ref-ie7-new-tab-insert.gif.motion_kind_basis: a one-shot state change: the stub becomes a tab and the row re-lays out; nothing travels or scales

ref-ie7-new-tab-grow.gif.game: Deterministic render of the target toolbar (muse-runs/ie7-newtab, render_animation.py MODE=grow)
ref-ie7-new-tab-grow.gif.platform: synthetic reference built from the source toolbar pixels
ref-ie7-new-tab-grow.gif.element: the blank New Tab stub is pressed (100 ms tint), then stretches into the full second tab over 400 ms ease-out while the fresh stub slides right on its edge; the page icon and 'Connecting...' fade in as the tab widens; label swaps to 'Blank Page' in one frame
ref-ie7-new-tab-grow.gif.kind: SYNTHESIZED motion reference: the toolbar pixels are the real source, the second tab is a polygon copy of its first tab, the glyphs are Muse-generated; built so the model sees the intended motion on the exact target pixels

ref-ie7-new-tab-grow.gif.hold_ms: 1500 hold; 100 press; 400 tween; label swap at 2900; hold to 6000
ref-ie7-new-tab-grow.gif.cadence_basis: Chrome 1.0 (2008) tab-strip insert: the new tab's width tweens from the insertion point while neighbours re-lay out (see docs/research/ie7-era-browser-tab-motion.md §3)
ref-ie7-new-tab-grow.gif.motion_kind_basis: the stub changes size in place into the tab

ref-ie7-new-tab-slide.gif.kind: SYNTHESIZED motion reference: the toolbar pixels are the real source, the second tab is a polygon copy of its first tab, the glyphs are Muse-generated; built so the model sees the intended motion on the exact target pixels

sources.note: renderer; timings are constants at the top

ref-ie7-new-tab-slide.gif.cadence_basis: a period-adjacent alternative to the width tween: an element moving to its position while keeping its shape
ref-ie7-new-tab-slide.gif.motion_kind_basis: the tab moves to a new position keeping its shape

skipped.ref-card-flip.gif: No real flip frames obtainable: poketcg's card animations (anims3.asm AnimData158–163) are shuffle translations, not flips, and The Spriters Resource sheet downloads were not fetchable. Nothing was fabricated.

motion_kinds.translate: an element moves to a new position, keeping its shape
motion_kinds.rotate: an element turns about an axis in place
motion_kinds.scale: an element changes size in place
motion_kinds.reveal: an element changes state or is uncovered, one-shot
motion_kinds.blink: an element is substituted for another with no movement

motion_kind_rule: A run's reference must share the brief's motion_kind. Observed 2026-08-30: a magnifying glass asked to travel across a bust was given ref-coin-spin (rotate) as its reference, and the glass tumbled and changed size instead of travelling. The reference teaches cadence AND the kind of movement; the wrong kind is worse than none.
